item.title: Chart Rewind: In 1976, Merle Haggard’s Bicentennial ‘Freedom Train’ Rolled
item.description:
[Energetic music fades out, and the host begins speaking]
Host: "Welcome to this week's episode of 'Trending on Billboard'. We're taking a trip down memory lane to 1976, when America was celebrating its Bicentennial. As part of the festivities, a song called 'Here Comes the Freedom Train' was recorded by the one and only Merle Haggard. Written by Stephen H. Lemberg, this patriotic tune used railroad metaphors to tell the story of America's past, featuring notable figures like George Washington, Benjamin Franklin, and Martin Luther King."
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: "Released on April 1, 1976, 'Here Comes the Freedom Train' entered Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart in May and peaked at number 10 on July 4. But what's interesting is that Merle Haggard wasn't the first to record this song. Porter Wagoner and Dolly Parton had teamed up with Chet Atkins to record it earlier, but Haggard's version was the one that made it to radio and retail."
[Music transitions to a more contemporary tune]
Host: "Fast forward to today, and we're celebrating America's Semiquincentennial. Country artists like Trace Adkins and Gretchen Wilson are getting in on the action. Trace will be performing on PBS' A Capitol Fourth: 250th Weekend Celebration on July 3, while Gretchen will be taking part in the Freedom 250 National Memorial Day Candlelight Tribute at Arlington National Cemetery on May 25."
[Music fades out, and the host wraps up]
Host: "That's all for this week's episode of 'Trending on Billboard'. Join us next time for more music news and interesting facts from the world of country music."
